topic_title: Top 10 Calming Dog Breeds for People With Anxiety
intro: For an anxious owner, the right dog lowers the load on a hard day rather than adding to it. Noise matters first, because a dog that barks at every sound keeps the household on edge. Energy comes next: a breed that needs two hours of hard exercise becomes a source of guilt when you are struggling. Look for affectionate, gentle breeds that enjoy close contact, are easy to train and get along with other people and pets. A dog can be good company, but it is not a substitute for professional care.

picks.description: The Standard Schnauzer is the least obviously calming breed here, but it suits anxious owners who find steady structure and a confident, loyal dog reassuring. It is intelligent, alert and easy to train, and good with children, cats and other dogs. Our data rates it medium energy, so 45 to 60 minutes of walks and play daily plus training keeps it settled. Its alertness has two sides: it watches over the home, but it may bark at noises and needs a consistent quiet cue. The wiry coat sheds little but needs weekly brushing and hand-stripping or clipping every couple of months. It is a medium-sized, long-lived dog at 13 to 16 years. Confident, clear handling works better than an anxious, inconsistent approach.
picks.best_for: Owners who value a loyal, watchful dog and enjoy daily training
picks.quirky_fact: Standard Schnauzers were once used as guard dogs for farm carts and stables in Germany.
picks.skip_if: Sudden barking unsettles you or you want a mellow lap dog

picks.description: The Finnish Lapphund is a medium-sized herding dog with a notably calm, friendly and affectionate temperament for its group. It is easy to train, good with children, cats and other dogs, and needs about 45 to 60 minutes of daily exercise, including some free play or training games. The thick double coat suits cold climates but sheds heavily and needs brushing a couple of times a week, with a heavy seasonal shed. Our data rates the breed medium for barking, and as a former reindeer herder it may bark to alert or to move things along. Lapphunds handle heat poorly. They are rare outside the Nordic countries, so finding a puppy can take time. Lifespan is around 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Owners in cooler climates wanting a calm, medium-sized companion
picks.quirky_fact: Lapphunds were bred by the Sami people of northern Finland to herd reindeer.
picks.skip_if: You live somewhere hot, want low shedding, or need a puppy quickly

picks.description: The Boston Terrier is a friendly, compact dog that suits owners who want companionship with very little upkeep. The short, smooth coat sheds little and needs only a weekly wipe or brush, and 30 to 45 minutes of walks and play a day is enough. Bostons are easy to train, good with children, cats and other dogs, and tend to be playful and clownish, which can help on low days. Our data rates them medium for barking, and some are excitable around visitors. The short face brings trade-offs: snoring, poor heat tolerance and a risk of breathing and eye problems, so keep walks short in hot weather and choose a breeder focused on health.
picks.best_for: Owners who want a playful, low-grooming dog in a small home
picks.quirky_fact: The Boston Terrier was one of the first breeds developed in the United States.
picks.skip_if: You live somewhere hot without air conditioning or want a quiet sleeper

picks.description: The Whippet is quiet, gentle and affectionate, and our data rates it low for barking and low for shedding, which makes it one of the calmest homes to share. It needs a burst of exercise, ideally a safe, fenced sprint and a 30 to 45 minute walk a day, and then it sleeps much of the day, often under a blanket. Whippets are easy to train with gentle methods but are sensitive, so harsh corrections backfire. They are good with children, cats and other dogs in our data, though their strong chase instinct means small animals outdoors can trigger a sprint, so keep them leashed in open areas. The short, smooth coat needs almost no grooming. They feel the cold and usually need a coat in winter.
picks.best_for: Calm households wanting a quiet, low-shedding, medium-sized companion
picks.quirky_fact: Whippets can reach around 35 miles per hour, yet are known indoors as dedicated couch sleepers.
picks.skip_if: You can't provide a safe fenced area or keep a dog leashed outdoors

picks.description: The Maltese is the only breed here rated low for energy, which makes it a fit for owners who want a calm, small companion without long daily walks. Twenty to thirty minutes of short walks and indoor play is usually enough. It is affectionate, gentle and easy to train, and good with children, cats and other dogs, though at toy size it is fragile with rough handling. The long, silky white coat sheds little but needs daily brushing or a short puppy clip every four to six weeks, plus routine eye and tear-stain cleaning; some owners find this grooming soothing, others find it a chore. Our data rates it medium for barking, so teach a quiet cue early. Maltese often live 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a tiny, low-energy dog that loves close contact
picks.quirky_fact: The Maltese has no undercoat, so it feels cold quickly and often needs a sweater in winter.
picks.skip_if: You have very young children or don't want daily grooming

picks.description: The Cavalier is the best match for anxious owners in our data: affectionate, gentle, calm and rated low for barking, so it rarely startles a household. It is small at 13 to 18 pounds and happy with 30 to 45 minutes of gentle walks and play, then long stretches on a lap or beside you on the sofa. Cavaliers are easy to train and get along with children, cats and other dogs, which makes visitors and shared spaces easier. The silky coat sheds moderately and needs brushing a few times a week. The two real drawbacks are dependence and health: Cavaliers dislike being left alone for long, and the breed has a high rate of heart disease, so choose a breeder who health-tests parents.
picks.best_for: People who are home often and want a quiet, affectionate lap dog
picks.quirky_fact: Cavaliers are toy spaniels and keep a spaniel's nose, so many enjoy short sniffing walks more than fast ones.
picks.skip_if: You work long hours away or can't handle possible ongoing vet costs

picks.description: The Havanese is a sturdy small dog built for companionship: affectionate, gentle, playful and easy to train. It follows its people from room to room, which many anxious owners find comforting, though the same trait makes it prone to separation distress when alone for long. About 30 minutes of walks plus indoor play covers its exercise needs. It is good with children, cats and other dogs. The long, silky coat sheds little but tangles easily, so expect brushing most days or a shorter trim every six to eight weeks. Our data rates the breed medium for barking; it may announce visitors, so early quiet training helps. The Havanese is one of the longer-lived breeds here at 14 to 16 years.
picks.best_for: People who work from home and want a constant, gentle shadow
picks.quirky_fact: The Havanese is the national dog of Cuba and is named after Havana.
picks.skip_if: You're regularly away for long hours or want minimal coat care

picks.description: The Newfoundland is one of the calmest, gentlest breeds in our data, rated low for barking and known for a patient, steady temperament. Just leaning against one can feel grounding. It needs only 30 to 60 minutes of moderate exercise daily and loves swimming. It is easy to train and good with children, cats and other dogs. The practical demands are large, though: this is a giant dog that often weighs well over 100 pounds, drools heavily, sheds a thick coat that needs brushing several times a week, and costs more in food, vet care and boarding. Its lifespan of 8 to 10 years is short. For owners with space and budget, it is a quiet, reassuring presence.
picks.best_for: Owners with space and budget wanting a calm, quiet gentle giant
picks.quirky_fact: Newfoundlands were bred to help fishermen haul nets and rescue people from cold water.
picks.skip_if: You live in a small home, dislike drool, or need low running costs

picks.description: The Bichon Frise is cheerful, affectionate and gentle, a small dog that tends to lift the mood of a room without being demanding. It needs about 30 to 45 minutes of daily walks and play and enjoys short training games, which it learns easily. Bichons are good with children, cats and other dogs. The curly coat sheds little but grows continuously, so plan for brushing several times a week and professional grooming every four to six weeks, which is a real ongoing cost. Our data rates the breed medium for barking. Bichons are people-focused and can develop separation distress if left alone for long workdays, and house-training can take longer than with larger breeds. They typically live 12 to 15 years.
picks.best_for: Owners wanting a small, upbeat, low-shedding and sociable companion
picks.quirky_fact: Bichons are known for the 'Bichon blitz', a sudden burst of fast laps around the room.
picks.skip_if: You're away most of the day or can't budget for regular grooming

picks.description: The Collie is a large, gentle and loyal dog with a calm presence that suits owners who want a bigger companion. It is easy to train, sensitive to its owner's mood and good with children, cats and other dogs. It needs 45 to 60 minutes of daily exercise, a moderate amount for its size. The trade-offs are coat and noise: the long rough coat sheds heavily and needs thorough brushing a few times a week, more in shedding season, and our data rates Collies medium for barking, with some prone to alert barking at noises. As a large dog it needs more space and food than the small breeds above. Collies can be sensitive to certain medications, so tell your vet the breed.
picks.best_for: Owners with space who want a gentle, intuitive large dog
picks.quirky_fact: Many Collies carry the MDR1 gene variant, which makes some common drugs riskier, and a simple test can check for it.
picks.skip_if: You live in a small apartment or can't keep up with heavy shedding

faqs.question: What is the best dog breed for someone with anxiety?
faqs.answer: On this list, the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel is the best overall fit: it is affectionate, rated low for barking, easy to train and gets along with children, cats and other dogs. The Whippet is a quieter, more independent alternative, and the Maltese suits people who want a very small, low-energy lap dog. The individual dog's temperament matters as much as the breed.

faqs.question: Is an emotional support animal the same as a service dog?
faqs.answer: No. In the United States, a psychiatric service dog is individually trained to perform specific tasks for a person with a disability and has public access rights under the ADA. An emotional support animal provides comfort by its presence and does not have those public access rights, though housing rules may differ. Ask a licensed mental health professional which, if either, fits your situation.

faqs.question: Can getting a dog make anxiety worse?
faqs.answer: It can, if the dog's needs exceed what you can give. Puppies need frequent toilet trips, chew everything and wake at night, and a barking or high-energy dog adds daily pressure. Many anxious owners do better with a calm adult dog from a rescue or breeder, where temperament is already known, and with a plan for help on difficult days.

faqs.question: Which calm breeds are best for apartment living?
faqs.answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel and Whippet are both rated low for barking and adapt well to apartments with daily walks. The Maltese, Bichon Frise, Havanese and Boston Terrier are small enough for tight spaces but are rated medium for barking, so plan early training. Giant breeds like the Newfoundland are calm but need far more room than most apartments offer.

faqs.question: How much time does a calming dog need each day?
faqs.answer: Even the low-energy breeds here need 30 to 60 minutes of walks and play daily, plus time for training, grooming and companionship. Most of these breeds are affectionate and dislike long stretches alone, so plan for a dog walker or daycare on long workdays. Regular walks also build a steady daily routine for the owner, which many people find helps.

seo_title: Calming Dog Breeds for People With Anxiety (2026)
answer: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, Whippet and Maltese are the strongest picks here: affectionate, gentle and rated low for barking or low for energy. The deciding factor is a calm household routine, so favor quiet, people-focused breeds whose daily needs you can meet without adding stress.
method: We filtered a 150-breed dataset for breeds with medium or low energy, easy trainability and good compatibility with children, cats and other dogs, then ordered them by barking level, calm and affectionate temperament, and how manageable their size and grooming are.
author: Elena Marsh
